content.title: Liquid Fuels
content.description: Liquid fuels are combustible liquids that produce heat energy on burning. They have high calorific value, are easy to transport, and are widely used in automobiles, industries, aviation, and power generation.

content.content: Among all liquid fuels, petroleum is the most important natural source of energy. It is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons obtained from underground reservoirs. Petroleum is refined to produce useful products such as petrol, diesel, kerosene, lubricating oil, paraffin wax, and bitumen.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Petroleum products are essential fuels for transportation, industries, thermal power plants, aviation, and petrochemical industries.
Liquid Fuels
Liquid fuels possess several advantages over solid fuels. They have higher calorific value, burn with less smoke and ash, require less storage space, and provide better combustion control.

items.question: High Efficiency
items.answer: Produce more heat with efficient combustion.

items.question: Easy Transportation
items.answer: Can be transported through pipelines, tankers, and containers.

items.question: Clean Burning
items.answer: Produce less smoke and ash than solid fuels.

content.content: Petroleum

Petroleum, also known as crude oil, is a naturally occurring dark-colored oily liquid mainly composed of hydrocarbons along with small amounts of sulphur, nitrogen, oxygen compounds, and mineral impurities.

content.title: Composition of Petroleum
content.content: Petroleum mainly contains paraffins (alkanes), naphthenes (cycloalkanes), aromatic hydrocarbons, sulphur compounds, nitrogen compounds, oxygen compounds, and traces of metallic impurities.
Refining of Petroleum

Refining is the process of separating crude petroleum into useful fractions based on differences in their boiling points. The process is carried out in a fractionating column by fractional distillation.
Petroleum Fractions
Cracking of Petroleum
Cracking is the process of breaking large, heavy hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, lighter, and more valuable hydrocarbons such as petrol, LPG, and alkenes by applying heat, pressure, or catalysts.

content.title: Need for Cracking
content.content: Cracking increases the yield of petrol from heavy petroleum fractions and improves the economic value of crude oil.
Types of Cracking

rows: Produces high-quality petrol with better yield

content.content: Moving Bed Catalytic Cracking

In the moving bed catalytic cracking process, powdered or pelletized catalyst continuously moves through the reactor along with heavy petroleum oil. The catalyst promotes the cracking reaction, producing lighter hydrocarbons with high octane value.
Working Principle

Heavy oil is mixed with a moving catalyst and heated. Large hydrocarbon molecules break into smaller molecules in the presence of the catalyst. Carbon deposits formed on the catalyst are removed in a regenerator by burning with air, and the regenerated catalyst is reused.
Advantages of Catalytic Cracking

items.question: Higher Petrol Yield
items.answer: Produces a larger quantity of petrol from heavy oils.

items.question: High Octane Number
items.answer: Improves fuel quality and engine performance.

items.question: Lower Operating Conditions
items.answer: Requires lower temperature and pressure than thermal cracking.

items.question: Catalyst Reuse
items.answer: The catalyst is regenerated and reused continuously.

items.question: Economical
items.answer: Provides better efficiency and higher profitability.

content.content: Applications of Petroleum Products

items.question: Transportation
items.answer: Petrol, diesel, and aviation fuel power vehicles and aircraft.

items.question: Industries
items.answer: Used in boilers, furnaces, and generators.

items.question: Petrochemical Industry
items.answer: Raw material for plastics, synthetic rubber, fertilizers, and chemicals.

items.question: Construction
items.answer: Bitumen is used in road surfacing and waterproofing.

content.content: Importance of Petroleum Refining

Petroleum refining converts crude oil into valuable commercial products with maximum efficiency. It improves fuel quality, increases petrol production, and supplies raw materials for numerous chemical industries.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Frequently asked questions include petroleum refining by fractional distillation, fractions obtained, cracking, differences between thermal and catalytic cracking, and the working of moving bed catalytic cracking.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Petroleum is the most important liquid fossil fuel.
Refining is carried out by fractional distillation.
Major fractions include LPG, petrol, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil, paraffin wax, and bitumen.
Cracking converts heavy hydrocarbons into lighter hydrocarbons.
Cracking is classified into thermal and catalytic cracking.
Catalytic cracking gives higher petrol yield and better octane number.
Moving bed catalytic cracking uses a continuously moving catalyst.
Catalyst regeneration removes carbon deposits and allows catalyst reuse.
